title: PHP
subtitle: The language that grew up with the web, as it is written today: typed, object-oriented and fast, from a first script to safe, tested, professional applications.
description: PHP is a general-purpose scripting language best known for building websites and web applications. It first appeared in 1995 as a small set of tools for personal home pages and grew into the language behind a large share of the web: WordPress, MediaWiki (the software that runs Wikipedia), online shops, and countless applications built with the Laravel and Symfony frameworks. Modern PHP (version 8 and later) is a very different language from the one its old reputation describes: it has strict type checking on request, enums, readonly properties, a just-in-time compiler, and a mature ecosystem of packages, standards and tools.

This course is for anyone who already knows what a variable, a loop and a function are: the Start level of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) or equivalent experience in any language. It begins with PHP's history and your first scripts, works through the core language, arrays and strings, classes, interfaces, traits and enums, and errors and exceptions, and ends with handling web requests safely (validation, escaping and prepared statements), Composer and the PSR standards, testing, the major frameworks, and a complete small project.

To run the code, install PHP from [php.net/downloads](https://www.php.net/downloads.php) or your operating system's package manager (on macOS, Homebrew; on Windows, the builds at [windows.php.net](https://windows.php.net/download/)); the official Docker image `php:cli` also works. There is no official online playground, but the community site [3v4l.org](https://3v4l.org/) runs a snippet on many PHP versions at once. Every complete program in these lessons was run with PHP 8.6 by Lumenary's test suite, and the output shown is the output it printed. The lessons were drafted with AI assistance and are awaiting review by a human computer scientist.

levels.title: Foundations
levels.summary: Install PHP and run scripts from the command line, then learn the core language: values, types and strict mode, control flow and match, functions, and PHP's all-purpose arrays and its strings.

levels.title: Practice
levels.summary: Model programs with classes, interfaces and traits, make illegal states unrepresentable with enums and readonly data, and handle failure with exceptions.

levels.title: Professional
levels.summary: Handle web requests and forms safely, work the way PHP teams do with Composer, the PSR standards, PHPUnit and static analysis, meet Laravel and Symfony, and build a complete project.
